reading.body:
Clay White is named on 5 AI lobbying filings, all filed through one firm, for a single client, The AI Policy Network Inc.

The pattern is narrow rather than broad. Five filings, one firm, one client. The eighteen bills listed are the bills those filings name, not eighteen separate engagements, and the data does not say which bill drew which filing. What it does show is a concentrated relationship: one lobbyist, one organizational channel, a set of AI-related bills moving through Congress in 2025 or later.

The disclosed prior government positions are staff roles for two members of Congress, Chris Stewart and Jason Chaffetz. The Lobbying Disclosure Act requires filers to list covered positions held in the prior twenty years, so this is a disclosure requirement being met, not an inference about influence. It matters for AI because the bills named here are the legislative surface where compute, data center siting, and power procurement rules would be written, and lobbying filings are one of the few public traces of who is working that surface.

What this does not tell the reader: whether any bill advanced, what positions were advocated, how much was spent, or whether the lobbying changed anything. It also does not cover the other lobbyist sharing this name, who has a separate record. The data is a roster of disclosed contacts, and nothing more should be read into it.
